images.caption: USS Oklahoma City (CLG-5): Plan view of guidance radars for the ship's RIM-8 Talos guided missiles atop her after superstructure, looking to starboard, taken while she was undergoing an inclining experiment at the Long Beach Naval Shipyard, California (USA), 19 October 1963. images.filename: RIM-2 Terrier missiles on USS Providence (CLG-6), 2 May 1962 (NH 98548).jpg
images.caption: The Commanding Officer of the U.S. Navy guided missile cruiser USS Providence (CLG-6), Captain B.D. Voegelin, points out the "E" award, with one hashmark, on her Mark 9 RIM-2 Terrier guided missile launcher, 2 May 1962. Looking on is Rear Admiral K.L. Veth, Commander Mine Force, U.S. Pacific Fleet and Commander Naval Base Los Angeles. As a Captain, Veth was Providence´s first Commanding Officer when she was commissioned in 1959. The hashmark represents the second missile "E" won by Providence in two years of fleet competition. In her first year she won the Cruiser Battle Efficiency "E" and the Margorie Sterret Battleship Award for the most outstanding cruiser in the Pacific Fleet. Photographed at Long Beach, California (USA).
images.alt: The Commanding Officer of the U.S. Navy guided missile cruiser USS Providence (CLG-6), Captain B.D. Voegelin, points out the "E" award, with one hashmark, on her Mark 9 RIM-2 Terrier guided missile launcher, 2 May 1962. Looking on is Rear Admiral K.L. Veth, Commander Mine Force, U.S. Pacific Fleet and Commander Naval Base Los Angeles. As a Captain, Veth was Providence´s first Commanding Officer when she was commissioned in 1959. The hashmark represents the second missile "E" won by Providence in two years of fleet competition. In her first year she won the Cruiser Battle Efficiency "E" and the Margorie Sterret Battleship Award for the most outstanding cruiser in the Pacific Fleet. Photographed at Long Beach, California (USA).

Ray (DD-971)?), the amphibious assault ship USS Tarawa (LHA-1) and the amphibious assault ship USS Essex (LHD-2). The decommissioned aircraft carrier USS Ranger (CV-61) is in a graving dock in the upper right.

The decommissioned aircraft carrier USS Ranger (CV-61) is in a graving dock in the upper right.

images.filename: Amidship detail of USS Perkins (DD-877) in November 1962.jpeg

Note the elaborate antenna mast fitted atop her DASH drone helicoter hangar.
images.alt: View looking forward from the helicopter deck of the U.S. Navy destroyer USS Perkins (DD-877), taken while the ship was undergoing an inclining experiment at the Long Beach Naval Shipyard, California (USA), on 15 November 1962, at the conclusion of her FRAM II modernization.
